title: Chapter 1045
text:
Squatting a corpse was a technical job.

In order to protect the young hearts of the players, there were many ways for the players to choose from. They could revive on the spot, revive in the nearest city or vehicle, revive in specially bound coordinates, and even go offline without reviving. At the same time, they could only revive at most ten times every six days in Galaxy, so it was very difficult to squat.

In his previous life, Han Xiao was fine even though he was reckless, and this was largely due to this method of revival.

However, even with such a harsh prerequisite, the players still enjoyed squatting corpses. The more common methods were kidnapping, forced landing, and so on. When the players were in combat mode, there was a limit to going offline, and there was a punishment for forcefully quitting. Thus, kidnapping was derived, bringing the target to the nearest revival location and surrounding them. Forcing a vehicle to land was the same, making the target revive in the same spot or in the nearest vehicle. However, none of these methods could completely solve the revival mechanism, and the difficulty was very high. Even if all the locations were blocked, the target would still need to cooperate and not go offline.

Therefore, in the end, there was only one prerequisite for squatting corpses, and that was the other party's head.

From the ID [What Can You Do About Me], Han Xiao could feel an unruly and reckless aura that could not be hidden. It was like a firefly in the dark, so bright and so outstanding.

In the post, this [What Can You Do About Me] was an army player, and he described his experience in detail.

"Just now, I was carrying out a solo errand mission in the free competition zone and came to a transit planet. I met a group of unfamiliar players from other organizations. When they saw me, they took the initiative to attack me without saying anything and beat me to death.

"I asked them why, and they actually said that they just didn't like me. I don't know about the others, but I couldn't take it, so I directly revived on the spot and fought them head-on. This group of people is really f * cking annoying. They really squatted and killed me over and over again, killing all my revivals for today. They even privately messaged me and mocked me. F * ck!

"I was eating hotpot and singing when I was suddenly beaten up. Who did I offend?! I've already posted the IDs of these bastards. Today, I'm going all out. Fans of China, everyone is my father today. With one arrow, thousands of troops will come to meet me. Please respond to my call and help me send my regards to their families. Let these bastards enjoy the baptism of positive energy! "

Han Xiao glanced at them. These IDs were obviously American players, and they were all Demons.

He scrolled down to read the replies and realized that the post had become a sea of joy.

[Whip on the Horse: I'm shocked. Grumpy Old Bro is recognizing his father on the spot Σ (っ ° Д °;) っ]

[Human Pile Driver: I was bullied? I'll help you vent your anger!]

[Heartless Iron Lady: Thirty-year-old keyboard warrior requesting to join the battle!]

[My Good Brother Can't Take It Anymore: I'm just having fun watching foreigners scold each other. If they really want to learn how to scold others, it's up to us.]

[Can't think of a funny ID: What are the first few monsters? I thought they were looking at Little Uncle. Why are there so many literati in this game?]

Other than these replies, there were also some army players who were also complaining. There were quite a few who had the same experience.

However, not everyone was so stubborn. Most of them were only attacked by players from other organizations without warning. Furthermore, their opponents were not only the Americans but also players from other countries. Furthermore, not all of them were guild members … It was as if they were specifically hunting the army players.

Han Xiao's heart skipped a beat as he thought about the reason.

It was probably because of the butterfly effect. In his previous life, there was no Black Star Corps, and everyone was scattered. However, the Black Star Corps was currently the largest faction among the players.

From the reactions of the players, this most likely had nothing to do with the NPC organizations. It was completely the actions of some players. It could be that some people were hostile to the army players, or it could be that the large foreign guilds were secretly working together.

Currently, tens of millions of players were flocking to the Flickering World and stepping onto the stage of the universe, which attracted the attention of the various organizations. Tens of millions of people were just a drop in the ocean to a Star Field, but if it was a group of Immortal Grade B Supers, it was a force that could not be easily ignored.

As part of the ecology of the universe, the actions of the players would affect others. Han Xiao's intelligence network reported that more and more organizations were beginning to delve into the characteristics of the players, and more people were trying to make use of the players. The three Universal Civilizations had also put the recruitment and research of the players on the agenda.

The Black Star Corps, which the foreign players wanted to join at all costs, also received more attention. Many organizations were very curious about the source of Black Star's influence among the Immortals. Although the Black Star was indeed very famous, they did not understand why the first choice of so many Immortals was the Black Star Corps.

However, there were also many players who went to other factions. Therefore, although the situation of the Black Star Corps was concerning, it was not that exaggerated. If they really took all the players into their faction, the dynasty would probably come knocking on their door the next day to question them.

"The other organizations did not target the army, but the players who joined them came to cause trouble first."

Han Xiao carefully read all the replies and found that the ones who hunted the army players the most were the American, Japanese, and Korean players.

While the other party attacked the army players, they also tried their best to avoid killing the army warriors. It was obvious that they were specifically targeting the players.

He suddenly thought of something and searched the forums again. Sure enough, he found some anonymous posts that were blocked because of their words. It was a group of players from the other organizations showing off that they had killed the army players and said that they were targeting the Black Star Corps. Furthermore, they were very arrogant and looked down on the Chinese players by name.

"Interesting. So, this is the method."

Han Xiao finally understood the cause and effect, and his eyes narrowed.

He was not unfamiliar with this method. It had also happened among the players in his previous life, and it had also appeared in Version 4.0.

This was a very insidious method, and the people behind it were definitely the big clubs. The method was to secretly organize a group of local players to hunt down the players of the target faction and then ridicule them on the forums, provoking the anger of the players of the target faction and provoking a war of words. Then, they would secretly lead the conversation to race, country, and region discrimination, igniting hatred.

The goal of this was to use the method of establishing hatred to manipulate the inclination of the local players to choose a faction.

The explanation was very simple. This was because the players that the clubs of the various countries could control were only their employees and some peripheral players. The normal players of the country made up the largest group, and their actions were not controlled by the clubs. Therefore, in his previous life, someone came up with an insidious method to provoke hatred between countries to influence the inclination of the normal players to choose a faction.

For example, if a faction had a million players, with 800,000 Chinese players being the majority, and 200,000 normal American players, then the American clubs would hunt down the Chinese players and taunt them, leading the Chinese players to curse at them. Then, they would do a double act to fan the flames and change the topic to hatred between different countries.

This way, the 200,000 normal American players of the faction would be unhappy and would be dragged into the war of words. Then, the clubs would continue to fan the flames and create opposition.

The result would be that a considerable portion of the 200,000 Americans would leave the faction due to their anger towards the Chinese players. Then, more normal American players would be angered by this war of words, and the number of Americans joining the faction would decrease significantly. This was an important method that the big clubs secretly used to manipulate the inclination of the normal players of the country. They would create hatred, use hatred, and increase the cohesion of the local players.

The reason for this was very simple. The clubs did not want the local players to work for the factions that the clubs of other countries were in. They only wanted the normal players to work for their own faction.

When there were more players in the same faction, the competition for the normal players would become greater. However, to the clubs, the local players represented cheap labor. When they came to their faction, whether it was for normal development or for national wars, as long as the clubs raised their arms, the normal players would respond and become free fighters.

Normal players wanted to experience the game easily, and the professional players were also worthy of respect. However, the clubs and official guilds were commercial organizations. Their goal was to obtain rankings and profits in the Pro League.

Therefore, after Version 4.0 was released in his previous life, the clubs led by the Americans began to use all kinds of dirty tricks to control the fans, causing the environment of the forums to deteriorate to a certain extent. This weakened the mainstream factions of the clubs of other countries, and in turn, strengthened themselves. To put it simply, they were stealing leeks.

Only a few clubs of other countries did not follow suit, and China was one of them.

In his previous life, China was very powerful in real life. In addition to some historical factors, they were often discriminated against by some idiots in other countries. Therefore, they were very cohesive. Now, most of the Chinese players were in the Black Star Corps, so there was even less of a need to use such dirty tricks.

Tsk tsk, the first time this trick appeared, it was against me. Moreover, it was the clubs of many countries working together.

Han Xiao thought about it and understood what these clubs were thinking.

It was just that there were too many foreign players entering the Black Star Corps, and some of the foreign clubs did not want the size of the army to continue expanding. Otherwise, the army would have too much of an advantage in the faction competition. Not only would it suppress the development space of the other factions, but it would also allow the Chinese clubs to pick up a wave of labor for free. To the foreign clubs, this was equivalent to helping the enemy. Even during a national war, the normal players of these countries might not respond to the call due to faction restrictions.

As expected, because the army is too outstanding, the Chinese clubs have become the target of public criticism. Although those foreign clubs are not targeting me personally, if they continue doing this, my leek field might shrink.

After understanding this point, Han Xiao did not panic at all. Instead, he laughed.

Isn't this a good opportunity for me to increase the sense of belonging of the army's newcomers?

The reason why the Horde and Alliance were so cohesive was because of the background story and game settings, but the more direct reason was because the players of the two factions were fighting each other.

Setting up a target was a good way to quickly increase the cohesiveness of the group!

Discrimination that involves real life factors is an internal problem of the players. With my current identity, I really can't deal with it. However, I can target the main factions that the foreign clubs are in.

You guys control the country, I'll control the faction.

When the foreign clubs organize people to hunt down the army players, it's basically a matter of love. The faction will not give any rewards, so in their eyes, this is only an internal matter of the players.

Then, if I issue a bounty mission, and as long as the army players kill the players of your faction, I'll give them a reward. From the perspective of faction policies, the army players will be able to get rid of their passivity and organize a targeted counterattack. Then, what will happen?

At that time, even the normal players of the club countries will happily go and f * ck you up!

With the few people that the club secretly hired, how can they compare to the eight million warriors of the army?

If you play dirty, I'll kill you!

Hehe, since you guys don't want to focus on your development and can't stand the loneliness, playing these dirty tricks all day long, let me add fuel to the fire and make your careers even more prosperous.

With that in mind, Han Xiao smirked. He sat up from the lazy god seat, opened the faction interface, and started to draft the bounty mission.

…

At the same time, in an encrypted player chat channel, the executives of the professional club guilds of many countries were online.

Among them were America's Devil Club and Key Club, Japan's Hydra, Amaterasu, and Werewolf Club, Korea's Kimchi, Samsung Bomb Club, Italy's Classic and Pizza Club, Southeast Asia's Red Bay, Archipelago, Titan Club, and so on … It could be said that more than half of the regulars of the international arena were in the channel.

At this time, the topic that these club executives were discussing was related to the Black Star Corps.

Just as Han Xiao expected, as more and more players from various countries jumped ship to the Black Star Corps, these guilds that did not plan to change factions could not sit still anymore. They secretly worked together to curb the expanding player population of the Black Star Corps.

"… The people we've organized are acting according to plan. We're still preparing for public opinion, and the players' emotions still need to be brewed," the American Key Club executive said.

"The conditions are actually in our favor. China has won the Pro League consecutively, and this is their pride. They naturally have a sense of superiority, so we can influence public opinion and let the Chinese players talk about us. We can then make the normal players of various countries deliberately target us because our team's results are not good. We can let the Chinese players mock us. This way, we can attract hatred."

"Actually, this method is quite easy to see through. People nowadays are very smart …"

"Don't worry, players will be players. As long as they get carried away, the cause is not important. The Pro League is a very good entry point. It's easy to influence their emotions."

"Let's hope it works. We belong to different factions, and the biggest threat now is the Black Star Corps. There are just too many players there. If we don't weaken them, the advantage of the Chinese clubs will be too scary."

"It's best to isolate them this time."

Many of the executives discussed at once.

As for the attitude of the Black Star Corps, it was not within their consideration at all. To them, this was a matter between the players, and the NPC faction was just a decoration.
